findings.summary: A CLI test that runs the real accept_request text through the gate is missing from the dependents list, and the plan's fixture repair cannot fix it.
findings.evidence: tests/proposals.rs `athena(fx)` uses `Scenario::default().script()`. The default reading has two criteria: 'README.md ends with a greeting line' and 'the tests still pass' (common/mod.rs:364-365). `accepting_submits_a_job_that_lists_defaults_toml_and_edits_nothing` calls `athena.accept_proposal(..).unwrap()`. That calls `self.ask(&accept_request(..))` (proposals.rs:642), which reaches `refusing_check` in reading.rs:722. The plan reads every dash bullet when no Acceptance opener exists. accept_request writes four bullets ('Add the default with id = ...', 'Set version to ...', 'Set its source to cite the proposal's records: ...', 'Leave every other entry as it is.'). None shares a stem with the default criteria, so the reading is refused and the unwrap fails (the test also asserts JobState::Proposed). The dependents list cites only reading.rs `scope_limit_proposal_apply_shape` and the corpus for this shape. Step 8's repair, changing the request bullet, does not apply because accept_request generates the text. This is also a production change: real defaults-proposal readings must now cover all four bullets, and the bullet 'Set its source to cite ... records' points readers toward records/ paths that check_reading_references refuses. Fix: Add tests/proposals.rs (accepting_submits..., and any other test that calls accept_proposal) to the dependents and the files list. Name the repair: give that test its own `scenario.reading` with criteria covering the four accept_request bullets, plus deliverables that pass the earlier checks; no verdict is needed because the job is only Proposed. Add a corpus Accept case built from the full `accept_request(&ProposalRecord)` text with a realistic reading. State in the changelog that defaults-proposal readings must now cover each bullet.
findings.location: Dependents (request text shape with no Acceptance opener); crates/athena-cli/tests/proposals.rs:87-88, :208-242; crates/athena-core/src/proposals.rs:442-450, :642

findings.summary: A deferral matched by stem overlap refuses a part even when a criterion covers it, so ordinary narrowing sentences become false refusals.
findings.evidence: Step 5 lists each item as 'uncovered or deferred'. A clause defers an item when it has a deferral phrase and 'names the item by marker or by own-stem overlap'. Only out_of_scope items get the narrowing exception, and the overlap threshold for deferral is never defined. Counterexample: request part '(2) show the timeout in athena status'. The reading has a criterion covering (2) and the summary says 'colouring the status output is left for a follow-up job'. That clause shares stems with (2) ('statu', plus 'athen' if named), so the reading is refused even though (2) is covered and only an extension is deferred. Readings often defer follow-on refinements this way. This raises the newly refused share against the 10% hold limit, which the plan cannot measure before verification. Fix: Let a stem-overlap deferral refuse an item only when no criterion covers it. A deferral that names the item's marker (or restates all its own stems, as already proposed for out_of_scope) refuses even a covered item. Define the deferral overlap threshold in the comment. Add a corpus Accept case where a covered part has a deferred extension sharing two stems, plus the existing Refuse twin with the marker named.

findings.summary: The drain tests built on `complete_request` will certainly be refused, but the plan treats their edit as conditional.
findings.evidence: `complete_request` (drain.rs:6319-6321) produces the bullet '{path} is edited', e.g. 'crates/u1/lib.rs is edited'. Its distinctive stems are 'crate' and 'edite'. Neither appears in the default Scenario criteria. lowered_urgent_order (:6335), drain_order_equals_plan_order (:6394) and drain_order_follows_the_plan_as_the_queue_changes (:6440) drain these items through `Scenario::default()`, so the reader runs and the new check refuses. Some order assertions may still pass while items fail, which would hide the change. Fix: List these tests as known refused dependents. Commit the bullet change in `complete_request` (for example '- README.md ends with a greeting line'), and say which assertions show the items still run and land.
findings.location: Files: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (CONDITIONAL); Dependents entry for drain.rs:4681/:6320

findings.summary: The fake reader's copied bullets can be refused by checks other than check_scope_limit.
findings.evidence: `reader_turn` declares only FAKE_DELIVERABLE (fake.rs:312). A copied bullet that names a repo path absent from the snapshot is refused by check_reading_references (checks.rs:408-473), which reads content criteria. Copied text also passes through the boundary and criteria-evidence checks. The plan names only check_scope_limit as a limit. Generators feed the deterministic fake their own bullets: hestia root-cause requests (hestia.rs:1044-1056), structural_text (code_health.rs:520-558) and accept_request. Fix: Have the fake reader cite the marker for numbered parts ('(N): <part text>'), and drop path tokens from copied bullet text or keep only words. In the risk, list check_reading_references and the other checks a copied bullet can trip, and add one end-to-end case for a hestia-shaped request.
findings.location: Step 7; Risks (fake reader copies request bullets)

findings.summary: Marker citation can match an incidental `(3)` and cover a part by accident.
findings.evidence: The plan says 'digit-bounded' only. A criterion such as 'refusing_check returns Some(3)…' or 'the parser reads parts (1)-(3)' would cite (3), or (1) and (3), and cover those parts outright regardless of content. Such a mistake lets a reading pass, so it would go unnoticed. Fix: Count a marker citation only when the marker starts the criterion or stands as its own token (not after an identifier character), and not inside a range. Pin the cases 'Some(3)' and '(1)-(3)' in the marker_refs unit test.

summary: I read the plan and the code it names: checks.rs refusing_check, fake.rs reader/producer/verifier, common/mod.rs, job_plan.rs, drain.rs, proposals.rs, code_health.rs, hestia.rs and the corpus helpers. The plan fits the reading, and most cited seams exist as described: the new step goes last after check_reading_references, the fake verifier derives its verdict from the brief's criteria, verdicts are matched to criteria by index, and the job_plan.rs bullet repair is sound. Two major problems remain. First, crates/athena-cli/tests/proposals.rs runs the generated accept_request text (four dash bullets, no opener) through the gate with the default Scenario reading. The new check will refuse that reading, the dependents list omits the test, and the plan's repair of changing a request bullet cannot apply to generated text. It also changes the real defaults-proposal flow without saying so. Second, a deferral found by stem overlap refuses a part even when a criterion covers it, so a reading that defers only an extension of a covered part is refused. That is an obvious source of false refusals against an unmeasured hold limit. Minor issues: the complete_request drain tests will certainly be refused, not just possibly; the fake reader's copied bullets can trip check_reading_references; and marker citation can match an incidental '(3)'. Verdict: revise.
